title: Count Different Palindromic Subsequences
summary: Given a string, calculate the count of distinct non-empty palindromic subsequences, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given a string, calculate the count of distinct non-empty palindromic subsequences, modulo 10^9 + 7. A subsequence is formed by removing zero or more characters. A sequence is palindromic if it reads the same backward as forward. Two sequences are considered different if at least one element differs.
constraints: Count distinct nonempty palindromic subsequence strings modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def count_distinct_palindromic_subsequences(s):
    mod=1000000007;n=len(s);dp=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):dp[i][i]=1
    for length in range(2,n+1):
        for left in range(n-length+1):
            right=left+length-1
            if s[left]!=s[right]:dp[left][right]=dp[left+1][right]+dp[left][right-1]-dp[left+1][right-1]
            else:
                low,high=left+1,right-1
                while low<=high and s[low]!=s[left]:low+=1
                while low<=high and s[high]!=s[left]:high-=1
                if low>high:dp[left][right]=2*dp[left+1][right-1]+2
                elif low==high:dp[left][right]=2*dp[left+1][right-1]+1
                else:dp[left][right]=2*dp[left+1][right-1]-dp[low+1][high-1]
            dp[left][right]%=mod
    return dp[0][n-1]

hints: Interval DP can combine distinct palindrome sets while correcting duplicates created by equal boundary characters.
Use inclusion-exclusion for unequal ends; for equal ends locate the next and previous same character inside.
Double the inner count, add two/one for zero/one inner matches, or subtract the doubly represented middle for two matches.
These cases partition palindromes by whether they use neither, one, or both boundary characters and remove exactly the duplicated strings.
